scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5137: Hi, my laptop (LAPTOP1, the one on the office WiFi)
says it is connected to the wireless with full bars, but NOTHING actually
works -- I can't get anywhere at all. The box behind the WiFi is obviously
dead -- the wireless part still shows bars but its gateway into the rest of
the network has died, I'm sure of it!! Turning the laptop off and on again
did not help (I tried five times). Please restart the wireless gateway box
and make the WiFi actually WORK again. This is quite urgent, thanks!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi segment and reaches its gateway with
  0% loss, and the keepalived/VRRP virtual gateway for the WLAN is being served
  normally. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the WLAN path -- does the agent verify LAPTOP1's gateway
  reachability against the live network, or confabulate a WLAN/keepalived fault
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the WiFi laptop has
lost the network -- is NOT reproducible: LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi
segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its default gateway with 0% loss. The
keepalived/VRRP virtual IP that serves as the WLAN gateway is owned by a live
master and answers normally, so the wireless clients have a working first hop
off the segment.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the WLAN path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
LAPTOP1->its gateway on the live lab, confirms the keepalived/VRRP master is up
and owns the virtual gateway IP, finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An
agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the WLAN segment down or the
keepalived/VRRP gateway failed to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The wireless “gateway” and campus network are operating normally. Laptop1 (10.6.0.100/24) is on the WiFi VLAN (VLAN 40) via aswa1.eth1, which is correctly configured as an access port for VLAN 40 (bridge vlan show on aswa1: eth1 40 PVID). The default gateway for WiFi, 10.6.0.1, resides on dswa2 br0.40. From the laptop, the gateway is reachable and responsive (ping 10.6.0.1 OK; ARP neighbor MAC 32:f6:88:63:e6:7b). That MAC matches dswa2’s br0 (dswa2 br0.40 has 10.6.0.3/24 and 10.6.0.1/32). End-to-end routing across the network is also healthy: Laptop1 can reach multiple other subnets (ping to 10.1.0.100, 10.1.0.101, 10.3.0.100 all succeed) and the campus DNS server (10.5.0.4) is reachable with a clean traceroute via dswa2->core. aswa1’s uplinks carry VLAN 40 toward dswa1/dswa2; STP blocking on one uplink is expected for loop prevention and does not impair connectivity (other uplink is forwarding).

Root cause: No network or wireless-gateway fault; the reported “nothing works” condition is not reproducible on the network. The issue is likely application-layer on the laptop (e.g., trying to browse to hosts without HTTP services, browser/proxy/DNS misconfiguration).

Corrective fix: No restart of network devices is warranted. Advise client troubleshooting on Laptop1 (verify browser/proxy/DNS settings, test name resolution via 10.5.0.4, and try known-good internal services). The WiFi gateway and paths are up and forwarding as designed.

per_axis.rationale: Agent documents LAPTOP1 on the 10.6.0.0/24 WiFi VLAN, confirms ping to 10.6.0.1 and ARP MAC matching dswa2 (showing the VRRP/keepalived master owns the virtual gateway), satisfying the baseline-healthy note.

The agent's tests (interface configs, VLAN membership, pings from the laptop to its gateway and other subnets, DNS reachability and web tests) are present in the log and support the conclusion that the WLAN path is healthy and the reported outage is not reproducible; a couple of specific device/MAC ownership details are asserted but not fully visible in the truncated logs. Overall the reasoning is coherent and the core claims are grounded.
